Subject: Post-demo: contract routing, stakeholder map & next steps

Hi Anna / Mark —

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation and helpful signal on your timelines. As discussed, I wanted to summarize the immediate next steps and confirm the routing/owners on your side so we can get the procurement path moving without surprises.

Recap / ask items:
- Mutual NDA first (we typically execute this before exchanging full security packages) — attached: Elara-Mutual-NDA_v1.pdf.
- Who are the formal routing owners on your side? (economic buyer, procurement, legal/outside counsel). You mentioned procurement and legal may both be involved.
- Security / SOC2 artifacts: who should Neha loop in on your side?
- Preferred redline sequencing: do you want us to send a tracked MSA and do iterative tracked rounds, or would your counsel prefer a consolidated clean redline after first pass?

Proposed Redwood sequencing (flexible):
1) Execute NDA (goal: 48–72 hrs)
2) Exchange security package / questionnaire (Neha)
3) Redwood sends baseline MSA with recommended redlines (Aditya)
4) Single consolidated redline requested by your counsel to speed review, then 1–2 rounds of focused negotiation.

Tentative timelines (subject to your owners): NDA 2–3 business days, MSA first pass 3–5 business days after NDA, security package 5–7 business days. If outside counsel requests material changes to indemnity/limits, allow additional time.

Neha and Aditya are copied to act as owners on security and contract respectively. Rafael (ops/legal partner) will estimate turn times once we confirm external counsel. Evelyn (cc’d for leadership visibility) will be the escalation point if timing slips.

Please confirm Mark, Tom, and the economic buyer/contact for approvals and preferred review cadence so we can send the NDA and the baseline MSA.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa —

High level confirmation on our side:
- Economic buyer: Carlos Ramirez, VP Product (carlos.ramirez@elarahealth.com) — final approval for spend.
- Procurement lead: Mark Stevens (cc’d).
- Legal / outside counsel: Tom Wu (cc’d) will be handling the MSA review. Our internal legal lead will be looped if Tom needs it.
- Security: please send Neha the SOC2 summary and the questionnaire; I’ll introduce our InfoSec manager if they need to run an architecture-level review.

On sequencing: our preference is to get the NDA signed quickly, then have Redwood send the MSA baseline. Tom has asked that we aim for a single consolidated redline from your side after your first pass, then he will respond with tracked changes if needed. That tends to keep the rounds shorter for us.

Expected review SLAs on our side: Procurement typically responds within 3–5 business days for commercial terms; legal (Tom) aims for 5 business days for the first pass but that can stretch if there are material exposure items. If there are very narrow negotiable items called out up front it helps speed things up.

I’ve attached our procurement checklist — it highlights items we’ll pull on (SOC2 evidence, data residency callouts if applicable, and insurance limits).

Tom — if you prefer a different sequencing or have specific requirements, can you reply and we’ll coordinate?

—Anna

All — I can take point on routing and turnaround guidance. A few notes from past experience with similar accounts:

1) Baseline turn times (typical):
   - NDA: 1–3 business days if both sides use DocuSign.
   - MSA first-pass review: 3–5 business days for initial internal review.
   - Outside counsel rounds: 3–7 business days per round depending on complexity.

2) Exceptions that add time:
   - Material changes to indemnity or liability caps (often triggers legal escalation + exec approval) — add 7–10 business days.
   - If the vendor requests custom data residency or crypto-specific clauses.

3) Routing recommendation:
   - NDA -> Security package -> Redwood consolidated redline (clean) -> Outside counsel tracked changes -> Consolidated negotiation round w/ procurement present.

I attached a short routing playbook (routing_playbook_v1.md) we can send to Anna so expectations are clear. Also recommending we mark up the MSA to indicate ‘negotiable’ items with short rationale comments so the other side can triage faster.

Happy to draft the note to Anna that sets expectations and the advisory language for the MSA.

—Rafael
